sanskrit_verse:
योऽभियुक्तः परेतः स्यात् तस्य रिक्थी तमुद्धरेत् ।
न तत्र कारणं भुक्तिरागमेन विनाकृता ॥२.२९॥
transliteration: yo'bhiyuktaḥ paretaḥ syāt tasya rikthī tam uddharet | na tatra kāraṇaṃ bhuktir āgamena vinākṛtā || 2.29 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When one who has been appointed dies before assuming possession, his heir shall reclaim that entitlement without delay; no consumption or enjoyment thereof is lawful without formal assumption.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through rightful assumption, not mere appointment.
Causation aligns with conscious engagement in dharma-duty.
Capacity-based responsibility requires actualization, not inheritance alone.
Restoration logic ensures continuity of dharma-function upon cessation of prior assignee.
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of unactualized rights as non-transferable until embodied.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a designated individual dies BEFORE executing the assigned function THEN the right reverts to the estate-holder for reassignment.
NO lawful claim arises from passive inheritance UNTIL formal initiation into the role occurs.
ANY act performed under unactivated authority SHALL be null and subject to reversal.
THE executor MUST verify assumption status PRIOR to recognizing any entitlement transfer.
RESTORATION OF FUNCTIONAL CONTINUITY takes precedence over static property claims.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes involving posthumous appointments or transfers of duties, the Court must recognize that authority is activated only upon conscious assumption. Mere nomination or inheritance does not confer legitimacy unless followed by initiation. The court's role is to ensure continuity of dharma-function while preventing unauthorized exploitation of unassumed roles.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that authority manifests through action, not title. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that entitlement follows activation, not death. Proportional responsibility lies in ensuring alignment between capacity and enactment. There is no fault where there was no assumption; thus, correction restores order rather than inflicts penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate immediate retrieval process of unclaimed entitlements.
Verify all preceding conditions of assumption were fulfilled.
Reassign the function according to current dharma-capacity mapping.
Integrate records to prevent future misalignment due to premature recognition.
Restore systemic balance by reaffirming the primacy of conscious assumption.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Authority is realized only through conscious assumption; inheritance cannot substitute embodiment. Dharma is restored when capacity meets function. Reality remains non-punitive, governed solely by the alignment of consciousness with duty. Thus it is declared.
